60: fn parse_name_value_opt<'a>(opts: &mut Options<'a>, opt: &'a OsStr) -> UResult<bool> {
61:     // is it a NAME=VALUE like opt ?
62:     let wrap = NativeStr::<'a>::new(opt);
63:     let split_o = wrap.split_once(&'=');
64:     if let Some((name, value)) = split_o {
65:         // yes, so push name, value pair
66:         opts.sets.push((name, value));
67:         Ok(false)
68:     } else {
69:         // no, it's a program-like opt
70:         parse_program_opt(opts, opt).map(|_| true)
71:     }

86: fn load_config_file(opts: &mut Options) -> UResult<()> {
87:     // NOTE: config files are parsed using an INI parser b/c it's available and compatible with ".env"-style files
88:     //   ... * but support for actual INI files, although working, is not intended, nor claimed
89:     for &file in &opts.files {
90:         let _ = EnvAppData::default().ingest_os_token(file);
91:         let conf = if file == "-" {
92:             let stdin = io::stdin();
93:             let mut stdin_locked = stdin.lock();
94:             Ini::read_from(&mut stdin_locked)
95:         } else {
96:             Ini::load_from_file(file)
97:         };
98: 
99:         let conf =
100:             conf.map_err(|e| USimpleError::new(1, format!("{}: {}", file.maybe_quote(), e)))?;
101: 
102:         for (_, prop) in &conf {
103:             // ignore all INI section lines (treat them as comments)
104:             for (key, value) in prop {
105:                 let _ = EnvAppData::default().ingest_text_pair(key, value);
106:                 env::set_var(key, value);
107:             }
108:         }
109:     }
110: 
111:     Ok(())
112: }

451:         &mut self,
452:         original_args: &Vec<OsString>,
453:     ) -> UResult<Vec<std::ffi::OsString>> {
454:         let mut all_args: Vec<std::ffi::OsString> = Vec::new();
455:         for arg in original_args {
456:             let _ = self.ingest_os_token(arg);
457:             match arg {
458:                 b if check_and_handle_string_args(b, "--split-string", &mut all_args, None)? => {
459:                     self.had_string_argument = true;
460:                 }
461:                 b if check_and_handle_string_args(b, "-S", &mut all_args, None)? => {
462:                     self.had_string_argument = true;
463:                 }
464:                 b if check_and_handle_string_args(b, "-vS", &mut all_args, None)? => {
465:                     self.do_debug_printing = true;
466:                     self.had_string_argument = true;
467:                 }
468:                 b if check_and_handle_string_args(
469:                     b,
470:                     "-vvS",
471:                     &mut all_args,
472:                     Some(original_args),
473:                 )? =>
474:                 {
475:                     self.do_debug_printing = true;
476:                     self.do_input_debug_printing = Some(false); // already done
477:                     self.had_string_argument = true;
478:                 }
479:                 _ => {
480:                     all_args.push(arg.clone());
481:                 }
482:             }
483:         }

485:         Ok(all_args)

488:     fn parse_arguments(
489:         &mut self,
490:         original_args: impl uucore::Args,
491:     ) -> Result<(Vec<OsString>, clap::ArgMatches), Box<dyn UError>> {
492:         let original_args: Vec<OsString> = original_args.collect();
493:         let args = self.process_all_string_arguments(&original_args)?;
494:         let app = uu_app();
495:         let matches = app
496:             .try_get_matches_from(args)
497:             .map_err(|e| -> Box<dyn UError> {
498:                 match e.kind() {
499:                     clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp
500:                     | clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayVersion => e.into(),
501:                     _ => {
502:                         // extent any real issue with parameter parsing by the ERROR_MSG_S_SHEBANG
503:                         let s = format!("{}", e);
504:                         if !s.is_empty() {
505:                             let s = s.trim_end();
506:                             uucore::show_error!("{}", s);

556:     fn run_program(
557:         &mut self,
558:         opts: &Options<'_>,
559:         do_debug_printing: bool,
560:     ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn UError>> {
561:         let prog = Cow::from(opts.program[0]);
562:         let _ = self.ingest_os_token(prog.as_ref());
563:         #[cfg(unix)]
564:         let mut arg0 = prog.clone();
565:         #[cfg(not(unix))]
566:         let arg0 = prog.clone();
567:         let args = &opts.program[1..];
568: 
569:         /*
570:          * On Unix-like systems Command::status either ends up calling either fork or posix_spawnp
571:          * (which ends up calling clone). Keep using the current process would be ideal, but the
572:          * standard library contains many checks and fail-safes to ensure the process ends up being
573:          * created. This is much simpler than dealing with the hassles of calling execvp directly.
574:          */
575:         let mut cmd = process::Command::new(&*prog);
576:         cmd.args(args);
577: 
578:         if let Some(_argv0) = opts.argv0 {
579:             #[cfg(unix)]
580:             {
581:                 cmd.arg0(_argv0);
582:                 arg0 = Cow::Borrowed(_argv0);
583:                 if do_debug_printing {
584:                     eprintln!("argv0:     {}", arg0.quote());
585:                 }
586:             }
587: 
588:             #[cfg(not(unix))]
589:             return Err(USimpleError::new(
590:                 2,
591:                 "--argv0 is currently not supported on this platform",
592:             ));
593:         }
594: 
595:         if do_debug_printing {
596:             eprintln!("executing: {}", prog.maybe_quote());
597:             let arg_prefix = "   arg";
598:             eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, 0, arg0.quote());
599:             for (i, arg) in args.iter().enumerate() {
600:                 eprintln!("{}[{}]= {}", arg_prefix, i + 1, arg.quote());
601:             }
602:         }
603: 
604:         match cmd.status() {
605:             Ok(exit) if !exit.success() => {
606:                 #[cfg(unix)]
607:                 if let Some(exit_code) = exit.code() {
608:                     return Err(exit_code.into());
609:                 } else {
610:                     // `exit.code()` returns `None` on Unix when the process is terminated by a signal.
611:                     // See std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt for more information. This prints out
612:                     // the interrupted process and the signal it received.
613:                     let signal_code = exit.signal().unwrap();
614:                     let signal = Signal::try_from(signal_code).unwrap();
615: 
616:                     // We have to disable any handler that's installed by default.
617:                     // This ensures that we exit on this signal.
618:                     // For example, `SIGSEGV` and `SIGBUS` have default handlers installed in Rust.
619:                     // We ignore the errors because there is not much we can do if that fails anyway.
620:                     // SAFETY: The function is unsafe because installing functions is unsafe, but we are
621:                     // just defaulting to default behavior and not installing a function. Hence, the call
622:                     // is safe.
623:                     let _ = unsafe {
624:                         sigaction(
625:                             signal,
626:                             &SigAction::new(SigHandler::SigDfl, SaFlags::empty(), SigSet::all()),
627:                         )
628:                     };
629: 
630:                     let _ = raise(signal);
631:                 }
632:                 return Err(exit.code().unwrap().into());
633:             }
634:             Err(ref err)
635:                 if (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound)
636:                     || (err.kind() == io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput) =>
637:             {
638:                 return Err(self.make_error_no_such_file_or_dir(prog.deref()));
639:             }
640:             Err(e) => {
641:                 uucore::show_error!("unknown error: {:?}", e);
642:                 return Err(126.into());
643:             }
644:             Ok(_) => (),
645:         }
646:         Ok(())
647:     }
